summary: Pilot scoping to define success criteria for a 4-week POC focused on prompt lifecycle, telemetry/telemetry retention, PII redaction, and bench targets. transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. 
[00:06] Maya Chen: Hey Alex, hi everybody. Sorry for the delay, had a quick stand.
[00:11] Priya Singh: Hi, Priya from Redwood SE. We'll pick up technical scoping today. We have a rough agenda: success criteria, traffic shape, PII concerns, benching plan and timeline.
[00:22] Raj Patel: Sounds good. For context, TierOne is evaluating a lending assistant that triages loan inquiries and drafts responses. We need to prove redaction, auditability, and cost predictability.
[00:34] Ethan Lo: Great. Quick housekeeping: recording on. If something's sensitive, flag it.
[00:38] Elena Ruiz: Quick note, our traffic will include SSNs, account numbers, some customer emails. We already token-masked at ingestion but prompts still carry free-text snippets.
[00:49] Priya Singh: Thanks. On the PII front, our standard approach in pilots is twofold: 1) client-side redaction with a configurable regex/PII-detector before send, 2) server-side prompt-hashing and optional ephemeral-only retention. We can show examples.
[01:06] Samir Desai: When you say "ephemeral-only retention" what's the default TTL? We need to know for compliance.
[01:12] Priya Singh: Default is no persistent prompt storage in the hosted flow unless you opt in—by default we keep a short telemetry shard for 24 hours for debugging, but that can be turned off or shortened in pilot. For Dedicated/Private installs, retention policy is in customer control.
[01:26] Maya Chen: 24 hours is okay as a starting point but we'll probably want 0 retention for PII-laden prompts. Can you support prompt redaction rules that remove numeric sequences that look like SSNs and bank numbers?
[01:38] Priya Singh: Yes. We have a redaction ruleset template — we'll share a sample config. Note that regex isn't perfect; we recommend a detection model step client-side then confirm with server-side patterns.
[01:49] Raj Patel: Also need KMS integration. We have AWS KMS managed keys and we need to ensure customer-managed key controls for logs and cache dumps.
[01:58] Alex Moreno: For Private and Dedicated, KMS integration is supported — we can plug your CMKs for persistent artifacts. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption; customer-managed KMS is available in Redwood Private. We'll capture that.
[02:11] Elena Ruiz: Benchmarks: we need to see p95 < 350ms for single-turn generation at our 1024-token average for top-tier cases. For bulk processing (batch scoring), throughput targets are different.
[02:24] Priya Singh: Helpful. Can you confirm expected QPS?
[02:27] Elena Ruiz: Peak 120 QPS for interactive; typical 30 QPS. Batch jobs will do 2K requests per minute during nightly processing windows.
[02:36] Alex Moreno: Ok, we'll model three workload classes for the POC: Interactive baseline (30 QPS, peak 120), High-concurrency (burst 300 concurrent requests with batching), and Batch scoring (2K/minute windows). We'll map to VM/GPU sizing and expected cost.
[02:52] Samir Desai: For benchmarking, what's your plan? We want apples-to-apples versus our current OpenAI endpoint.
[02:59] Priya Singh: We usually run a bench plan: baseline latency sweep, concurrency sweep, and end-to-end quality check using a curated prompt set. We'll run with your sample traffic; we also recommend fixed seeds and deterministic model variants for compare. We'll produce p50/p90/p95 and distribution plots.
[03:18] Maya Chen: On quality regression monitoring, we need to ensure prompt modifications (redaction) don't regress accuracy. How do you measure that?
[03:25] Priya Singh: Great question. We include a small evaluation harness: golden prompts + expected outputs. We score similarity (ROUGE/EM and also heuristic checks). For PII redaction, we recommend synthetic PII injection to verify redaction rules do not remove semantic content.
[03:41] Raj Patel: Regarding logs and audit: we need immutable audit logs for requests/response hashes, who accessed them, and RBAC. Do you capture admin audit events?
[03:49] Alex Moreno: Yes — Console and Private deployments include audit trails for admin actions, model rollouts, and API keys. For hosted, we provide detailed logs with token-level cost breakdowns but we can scrub payloads. Audit exports can be streamed to your S3 with encryption.
[04:03] Elena Ruiz: Does your telemetry include token counts per call and KV cache hits? We use those for costing estimates.
[04:09] Priya Singh: We can emit token counts, cache miss/hit rates, latency per stage, and per-model usage. Those are available via Console and a JSON export.
[04:18] Samir Desai: Any support for hashing prompts before storage so we keep only the hash that enables traceability without retaining plaintext?
[04:25] Priya Singh: Yes. We support HMAC hashing of prompts before they hit our storage. We can add a salt or client-side HMAC so only you can map hashes back. We'll include recommended code snippets.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Ok that sounds good. Success criteria: we'd like (1) p95 interactive latency under 350ms for 1024 tokens on comparable model, (2) verified PII redaction for 100% of synthetic tests, (3) telemetry exports with token and latency breakdown, and (4) cost-per-1K-token estimates within 15% of your forecast. Doable?
[04:56] Alex Moreno: Yes, that's exactly what we'll scope. We'll include these as pilot success criteria in the POC agreement.
[05:02] Raj Patel: Timeline — we want to run a 4-week pilot starting week of 2026-04-20. Phase 1 (week 1): integration and redaction rules, week 2: benching and initial quality checks, weeks 3-4: iterative tuning, and wrap and decision.
[05:19] Priya Singh: That timeline is realistic. We'll need your sample traffic and the access patterns asap to size the bench infra.
[05:26] Maya Chen: We'll try to get you an anonymized 7-day slice by Monday 2026-04-13.
[05:31] Alex Moreno: Perfect. On infra sizing, do we have any constraints on cloud region or VPC peering?
[05:37] Samir Desai: We'll want the pilot in us-west-2 and we'd prefer VPC peering for dedicated but for hosted we can do IP allowlists.
[05:46] Priya Singh: Noted. For a hosted pilot we can stand up the bench in us-west-2 and do IP allowlist. If it moves to Dedicated we can discuss VPC peering and private endpoints.
[05:55] Elena Ruiz: One more: logging retention requirements — we likely need 90 days for some operational logs but 0 days for plaintext prompts with PII. Can you set per-channel retention?
[06:06] Alex Moreno: Yes, retention is configurable per artifact type: telemetry metrics, admin audit logs, and raw payloads. We'll produce an initial config map for you to review.
[06:16] Raj Patel: Security scan: we may need a short security review call. I'll share our SOC2 checklist items; do you have a standardized security pack?
[06:24] Ethan Lo: We'll send the security pack and our SOC2 report. If you want a deep-dive, we can schedule a security-specific session with our security lead.
[06:32] Maya Chen: Good. Pricing: can you give a rough cost estimate for the pilot with the three workload shapes?
[06:38] Alex Moreno: We'll draft a cost table showing expected GPU-hours and estimated per-token cost for small (30 QPS baseline), medium (120 QPS peak), and large burst scenarios. That will be in the POC docs.
[06:49] Priya Singh: Anything else on the bench methodology? We usually run a warm-up period for KV cache priming, then three repeats per config to get stable p95. We'll include the raw results.
[06:59] Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Also include an A/B test with and without client-side redaction to measure quality delta.
[07:07] Priya Singh: Yes, we can include that in the matrix.
[07:10] Alex Moreno: All right, quick recap of action items: Redwood shares redaction playbook and example configs, the SE will send bench plan and test matrix, TierOne will provide anonymized traffic slice and confirm compliance checklist. Target start week 2026-04-20.
[07:23] Maya Chen: Thanks, that works.
[07:26] Raj Patel: I'll take point on compliance items.
[07:28] Alex Moreno: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench kickoff and the security deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
[07:35] Elena Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[07:36] End of recording.
